attribution: Franchise milestones for navigation and context. Dates are calendar or season labels as noted; verify before citing academically.

events.headline: Expansion birth
events.body: The NBA awards Minnesota a franchise; the Timberwolves begin play for the 1989–90 season, initially sharing the Hubert H. Humphrey Metrodome.

events.headline: Kevin Garnett arrives
events.body: The Wolves draft Kevin Garnett fifth overall straight out of Farragut Academy, setting the identity of the franchise for the next decade-plus.

events.headline: Target Center home
events.body: The club’s downtown Minneapolis arena becomes the long-term home after early seasons in the Metrodome.

events.headline: Western Conference finals
events.body: Flip Saunders guides Minnesota to the West’s top seed; Garnett wins MVP and the Wolves reach their only conference finals to date.

events.headline: Garnett traded to Boston
events.body: A blockbuster sends Garnett east; Minnesota pivots into a long rebuild around picks and young talent.

events.headline: Flip Saunders returns
events.body: Saunders comes back to the bench; his death in 2015 remains one of the organization’s most painful off-court chapters.

events.headline: Playoff drought ends
events.body: After 14 seasons without the postseason, the Wolves break through under Tom Thibodeau and Jimmy Butler—then quickly face roster drama.

events.headline: Chris Finch era begins
events.body: Finch takes over midstream and becomes the stabilizing coaching voice into Minnesota’s modern competitive window.

events.headline: Western Conference finals return
events.body: Anthony Edwards and company push deep in the playoffs, giving the franchise its first conference finals trip since 2004.
